predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: Macedonia round Thessalonica and Thessaly to Domokos, Pharsalus and Velestino, formed from the partition of Byzantine lands in northern Greece with Thessaloniki as its capital (Kingdom page)

successors.name: Despotate of Epirus
successors.text: Thessalonica and the rest of the kingdom, taken by Theodore Komnenos Doukas in December 1224

successors.name: Empire of Thessalonica
successors.text: Thessalonica, where Theodore 'soon after' declared himself emperor (Medieval Thessaly page)

rulers.name: Demetrius of Montferrat
rulers.title: King of Thessalonica (a child; regents: his mother Margaret of Hungary, then Eustace of Flanders from 1209/10)

ledger.x: 1204: Boniface of Montferrat founds the Kingdom of Thessalonica at Thessalonica.
1204-05: Boniface takes Thessaly to the Domokos-Pharsalus-Velestino line.
1205: the Lordship of Athens is a fief of the King of Thessalonica.
1205: Euboea is held of the King of Thessalonica.
1205: the Lordship of Salona is a vassal of Boniface (Kingdom page: the southern Greek principalities were Boniface's feudal vassals).
1205: the Marquisate of Bodonitsa is a vassal of Boniface (Kingdom page).
1209: Henry of Flanders ends the feudal dependency of duchy-of-athens on Thessalonica.
1209: Henry of Flanders ends the feudal dependency of the Triarchy of Negroponte on Thessalonica.
1209: Henry of Flanders ends the feudal dependency of Lordship of Salona on Thessalonica.
1209: Henry of Flanders ends the feudal dependency of Marquisate of Bodonitsa on Thessalonica.
1212: Epirus invades Thessaly.
1212: Larissa and central Thessaly pass to Epirus.
1218: Epirus presses into Macedonia.
1218: Platamon Castle surrenders to Theodore Komnenos Doukas.
Late 1221: Serres surrenders, cutting the road between Constantinople and Thessalonica.

c. 1222/3: the rest of Thessaly passes to Epirus. By then Theodore 'completed the recovery of the entire region except for Halmyros, which remained in Latin hands until 1246' (Medieval Thessaly); the year is approximate (1222 chosen, matching despotate-of-epirus /ledger 8). Halmyros is a 12 km disc.
c. 1222/3: the Thessalian fighting ends with Epirus holding the region except Halmyros (Medieval Thessaly).
December 1224: Thessalonica falls.
December 1224: the war for Macedonia ends with Thessalonica's surrender; Demetrius flees to Frederick II's court (Demetrius page).
December 1224: the Kingdom of Thessalonica falls to Epirus.

wars.name: Bulgarian war of Kaloyan against the Latins (Kingdom of Thessalonica's share)
wars.outcome: Boniface of Montferrat was ambushed and killed by the Bulgarians on 4 September 1207 and his head was sent to Tsar Kaloyan; the Kingdom page records no change of the kingdom's borders.

wars.name: Lombard rebellion against Henry of Flanders
wars.outcome: Henry advanced on Thessalonica in December 1208, crowned the child Demetrius on 6 January 1209 'extracting oaths of homage from the Lombard barons', and held a parliament at Ravennika; the feudal dependency of Athens, Bodonitsa, Salona and Negroponte on…

wars.name: Epirote conquest of the Kingdom of Thessalonica
wars.outcome: Michael I of Epirus attacked in 1210 and was beaten by Henry; he took Larissa and central Thessaly in 1212; Theodore took Platamon (1218), Serres (late 1221), the rest of Thessaly except Halmyros (c.1222/3), besieged Thessalonica from early 1223 and took it…

certainty.note: A feudal kingdom of fiefs whose edges the pages give only by towns: 'up to Domokos, Pharsalus, and Velestino' in the south; the eastern edge (Nestos) and the western Macedonian edge are Cliopatria's.
